Hi Samantha / Tom —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and suggested next steps so we can get you a concrete TCO and run the comparative benchmarks you asked for.

Call highlights (short):
- Primary use: high-volume document parsing + summarization for internal analytics (avg request size ~1.5k tokens, tail to 6k).
- SLAs: soft latency target ~300ms p95 for short prompts; acceptable batchy throughput for long contexts.
- Security: must support VPC/private deployment for any PII workloads.
- Current blockers: procurement wants clear per-1M token economics + comparison vs current hyperscaler spend.

Immediate next steps we propose:
1) Competitive benchmark: run same inference load against (a) Redwood hosted, (b) dedicated Redwood pool, and (c) your hyperscaler baseline (they mentioned Vertex + SageMaker in the call). We'll provide the harness.
2) TCO sheet: we attached a lightweight template to capture your current cost drivers (token counts, average latency, cache hit assumptions). Please populate and return.
3) Unit economics: we'll return per-1M token cost for common configs and the sensitivity to batching and cache hit rate.
4) Schedule: propose Wed 3/4 10am PT to align on test dataset and access (or suggest an alternate).

Attachments: 2026-03-03-acme-tco-template.xlsx (simple TCO input).

Questions for you before the test:
- Can you share a representative set of ~50 sample prompts + expected response lengths?
- Do you have constraints around keys/SSO for private testing?

I'll follow up after you send the sample data with a short benchmark plan and the cost sensitivities.

Thanks,

Samantha — thanks for the quick reply and the procurement doc. Per your ask, below is a concise per-1M token / TCO summary (ballpark, based on typical configs). We'll run the exact numbers once you return the TCO sheet and we run the harness against your samples.

Quick unit economics (assumptions: avg resp length 256 tokens, batching=8, cache hit=30%, model = open-llm-70B quantized variant where applicable):
- Redwood Hosted (standard): ~$6.5 per 1M tokens (includes serving + routing overhead). Assumes continuous batching=8, KV cache hit 30%, and moderate sequence lengths.
- Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity): ~$4.2 per 1M tokens (commit pricing, depends on utilization; higher cache hit and batching yield lower effective cost).
- AWS SageMaker endpoints (baseline): ~$12.0 per 1M tokens (varies by instance family; includes additional infra overhead we typically see in benchmarks).
- Google Vertex AI: ~$11.0 per 1M tokens (similar to AWS; lower network egress assumptions may vary regionally).
- Anthropic / API-based providers (comparable large-model APIs): ~$8.5–$10.5 per 1M tokens depending on model and concurrency.

Key levers and sensitivity notes:
- Batching: increasing batch size from 8->16 can lower per-token cost ~15-25% for throughput-bound workloads, but may increase p95 latency — we'll measure both.
- KV / prefix caching: increasing cache hit from 30%->60% reduces token compute by ~25–35% (depends on prompt reuse), which is the single biggest driver for real TCO gains for your workload.
- Dedicated pools: reserved capacity reduces unit costs significantly when utilization is sustained (>60%); we'll include a utilization curve.
- Hidden costs: network egress, auditing/retention, and long-context memory/kv storage can change effective TCO; we'll capture these in the TCO template.

Recommended next benchmark matrix (we'll run these against your sample set):
1) Baseline short: avg=2k tokens, batching=[1,8,16], cache_hits=[20%,50%,80%]
2) Long tail: avg=6k tokens, batching=[1,8], cache_hits=[10%,30%]
3) Dedicated vs hosted: run same load on a reserved Redwood pool tuned for throughput vs our hosted service.
4) Latency SLOs: measure p50/p95/p99 for each config.

Artifacts we'll share after initial run:
- Redwood benchmark plan + harness (attached).
- Per-1M token calc sheet populated with your numbers.
- Short slide summarizing tradeoffs and recommended deployment (hosted for POC, dedicated if long-term high utilization + private deployment needed).

Attachments: redwood-benchmark-plan.md (benchmark steps + harness link). Full benchmark harness and sample results will be shared on the Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-redwood/acme-bench

If that looks good I will confirm Wed 10am PT for the kickoff and Vivek will lead the test run.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
